stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Nm2x Image: Britta Pedersen/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement What you need to know about plague There are three forms of plague, all caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. The three forms of plague are bubonic, septicemic and pneumonic. Bubonic plague is the most common form, it does not spread from person to person. If untreated, the bacteria can move through the body and bloodstream, causing septicemic plague, which causes internal bleeding and organ failure. If the the bacteria reach the lungs, they cause pneumonic plague. Pneumonic plague is highly contagious as it can pass from person to person through the air, via coughing, for example. If untreated, bubonic plague kills between 30-60% of patients. The septicemic and pneumonic forms are always fatal without treatment. "The anger among young people didn't come out of nowhere," Lecornu said as he addressed the nation. The center-right prime minister said his government’s first policy responses to protesters’ concerns — including run-down schools, a shortage of substitute teachers, and a desire for more manageable schedules — would come later this month. The government will consider submissions on a public platform set up Tuesday to allow students to voice their grievances. Unions, teachers and left-wing political parties took to the streets in solidarity with high school students. But discontent in France extends beyond schools. A surge in fuel prices, triggered by the U.S.-led war in Iran, has added to concerns about the cost of living. stories.title: Ex-German intelligence chief arrested over suspected espionage

stories.article_text_excerpt: Former German intelligence chief August Hanning is accused of obtaining classified information from a former employee of the Federal Intelligence Service (BND) and using it in connection with his private consultancy work.Germany's Federal Prosecutor's Office is reportedly investigating the 80-year-old former BND president on suspicion of offences including obtaining state secrets and treason-related espionage.Hanning allegedly continued to receive confidential documents from the intelligence service for years after leaving office. His former chief of staff is suspected of supplying him with the material and has also reportedly been arrested.According to reporting by the "Süddeutsche Zeitung", the documents included intelligence reports intended for the German Chancellery.Investigators are also examining whether classified information was passed on to foreign powers.The investigation reportedly emerged from information uncovered during proceedings linked to German businesswoman Christina Block and the alleged leaking of documents from the Chancellery.The allegations are based on joint reporting involving the "Süddeutsche Zeitung" and German public broadcasters WDR and NDR.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters to rely solely on Rospotrebnadzor's statements.Between 189 and 197 of Shipilova's contacts were placed under observation and quarantine, according to figures cited by independent and regional media.Initial tests among those contacts returned negative. Chief among the abuses was the casting of ballots in the name of deceased voters who had lingered for years on outdated voter rolls. At just over 40%, turnout was the lowest since the Bosnian War ended in 1995, in part because the old tricks no longer worked. In earlier elections, allegations kept surfacing that votes were being cast in the name of people who had died or long since moved abroad. Others said voters cast their ballot multiple times or that blank ballots were added after polls closed to make the turnout look higher.
